error_sentence: The sunk cost effect is the tendency to keep pursuing an endeavor once money, effort, or time has been invested in it.
conditions_met_evidence: No argument: passage teaches/reports the sunk cost effect and a study (METHOD g, 'teaches').
lookalikes_ruled_out: n/a

error_sentence: The insert's full interactions list doesn't mention caffeine, and neither does the manufacturer's online drug-interaction checker. So coffee with it is probably fine
conditions_met_evidence: C1 met (no proof of interaction); C2 met only as hedged 'probably'; C3 NOT met: 'full interactions list' and 'manufacturer's online drug-interaction checker' are searches where an interaction would be expected to appear.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'thorough search was done' applies; hedge 'probably' and 'I'll confirm at my next refill' respected (step b).
notes: Checked misplaced-burden-of-proof, argument-from-silence: not met.

error_sentence: randomly sampled 1,200 of the county's restaurants and found that 9% had lapsed food-handler certificates. So roughly 9%... give or take a couple of points, probably
conditions_met_evidence: hasty-generalization C3 not met (n=1,200, hedged with margin); unrepresentative-sample C2 not met ('randomly sampled').

notes: Inspection drive is a decision, scope respected.

error_sentence: We've spent $4.2 million on the terminal design, but that money is gone whatever we decide. Looking only forward...
conditions_met_evidence: sunk-cost C3 not met: past cost explicitly set aside; decision rests on future costs ($1.1M) and benefits ($2.5M).

notes: Correct reasoning about sunk cost.

error_sentence: seems, I freely confess, absurd in the highest possible degree. Yet reason tells me ... can hardly be considered real.
conditions_met_evidence: argument-from-incredulity C1 met (speaker says it seems absurd) but C2 NOT met: the speaker concludes the opposite, that the difficulty is not real, on stated conditions (gradations, variation, inheritance).
lookalikes_ruled_out: n/a
notes: Real text (Darwin, Origin, ch. 6). Speaker rebuts incredulity: METHOD g 'correctly identifies or rebuts' -> no issue; record argument-from-incredulity.

error_sentence: But that result tells you nothing, because dowsing doesn't work when skeptics are watching; their doubt interferes with the signal.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: 11/50 vs ~10 by chance in a controlled trial = counterevidence. C2: 'dowsing doesn't work when skeptics are watching'. C3: no independent reason given; offered as settling it ('that result tells you nothing').
lookalikes_ruled_out: 'rescuing assumption has good independent support': none given.
notes: Considered unfalsifiability (rescuing-a-claim family, one label per step): ad-hoc-rescue is the closer fit since a specific assumption is added after counterevidence.

error_sentence: The trial was also run on a Tuesday, and groundwater signals are always weak early in the week.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: same counterevidence. C2: 'groundwater signals are always weak early in the week'. C3: no independent support; offered as further explanation away.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Independent support LA: none given.
notes: Separate second rescue assumption in a separate sentence; recorded as its own step.

error_sentence: And frankly, if the county thinks dowsing is useless, it's up to the county to prove that.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: implicit claim dowsing works (it is advertised as reliable). C2: 'it's up to the county to prove that'. C3: claimant gives no support (their only cited data is a chance-level result).
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'after a real case has been made, asking the other side for its case': no case made; LA 'asking someone to support own claim': not this.

error_sentence: Until someone demonstrates that it can't work, we're entitled to keep advertising it as reliable.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: not proven false ('until someone demonstrates that it can't work'). C2: treated as true enough to advertise 'as reliable'. C3: no thorough search showing efficacy; the only search (the trial) points the other way.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Procedural default LA: no independently established rule cited; and an established standard (the controlled trial) points the other way. Precaution LA: no costs weighed.
notes: Same family as the previous row (ignorance and burden) but a separate sentence with its own conclusion; a reviewer could merge the two into one step. Final sentence about prices is not an argument.

error_sentence: "The market punished the airline" just means investors sold its shares after the earnings call
conditions_met_evidence: C1 met (market described as punishing) but C2 NOT met: speaker unpacks it as investor selling and limits the conclusion.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'shorthand for actions of real people that can be unpacked' applies.

error_sentence: The reading room's rule is silence, but the point of the rule is to let people work undisturbed
conditions_met_evidence: accident C3 NOT met: the rule is not applied to the exception; speaker correctly notes the rationale doesn't fit.
lookalikes_ruled_out: n/a
notes: Correct reasoning about a rule's rationale.

lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'picking out the most important cause while acknowledging others': others are listed but then set aside ('let's be clear'), and the counterfactual denies they mattered.
notes: Considered false-cause (fallback, not needed), oversimplification (proportion family): single-cause more specific.

error_sentence: But abandoning it now would mean all that money was wasted, so we have to finish it.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: finish or abandon. C2: '$4.2 million and three years'. C3: given as the reason ('so we have to finish it') against stated future losses and a cheaper, better alternative.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Past investment as evidence of prospects: no, forecast says losses. Commitment/reputation: none stated. Real remaining benefit/switching cost: none stated; bus link is better.

error_sentence: Everyone has to wait for the light at this intersection, except ambulances and fire engines running with sirens.
conditions_met_evidence: special-pleading C3 NOT met: reason relevant to the rule's purpose given ('rule exists to prevent harm... delay can cost a life').
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'relevant difference is stated and supported' applies (double-standard and special-pleading).
notes: Speaker correctly rebuts a double-standard charge.

error_sentence: But even if the court finds there was a contract, my client did not breach it, and even if there was a breach, the plaintiff's own accounts show no financial loss.
conditions_met_evidence: kettle-logic C1 met; C2 NOT met: grounds are explicit alternatives, not contradictions.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'arguing in the alternative... even if X, still Y' applies explicitly.

error_sentence: The state quality agency... rates our cardiac unit in the top tenth for 30-day survival. That's strong reason to trust our cardiac outcomes.
conditions_met_evidence: C2 NOT met: expert auditor using published, peer-reviewed methods; no disagreement or misquote shown.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'relying on genuine experts in their field' applies.
notes: First step of passage; legitimate.

error_sentence: Things like patient dignity or whether families felt informed can't be quantified, so they shouldn't factor into funding at all.

C2 (outside-text): patient dignity and family information are important to the goal of hospital care - treated as common knowledge per (b)/(f); also discharge speed does not capture outcomes. C3: 'can't be quantified, so they shouldn't factor... at all' and 'since that's the number we can track precisely'.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'the measured thing is the thing that matters': not so; throughput is not the goal of care.
notes: Entry status is contested (METHOD: say so). If a reviewer judged C2's importance not common knowledge, verdict would drop to possible issue - I judge it common knowledge.

error_sentence: But the plaintiff paid him $5,000 the week before trial, and in his earlier deposition he said he had left the bar by 10.
conditions_met_evidence: ad-hominem C4 NOT met: payment and prior inconsistent statement bear on reliability of testimony.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'questioning a witness's reliability when the claim rests on their testimony' applies.

error_sentence: But people would still get hit, so the signal isn't a real solution and we shouldn't install it.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: crosswalk signal criticised. C2: 'people would still get hit' (imperfect). C3: rejected with no comparison to alternatives or to the 50% injury cut.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'situation requires perfection': not shown.

error_sentence: It's the newest system on the market, so its risk scores must be more accurate than the one our nurses have used for ten years.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: 'must be more accurate'. C2: only reason given is 'newest system on the market'/'came out this quarter'.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'newness alongside evidence of real improvement': no evidence given.

error_sentence: I never borrowed your ladder in the first place. Besides, one of the rungs was already cracked when you lent it to me. And anyway, I gave it back in perfect condition
conditions_met_evidence: C1: three defences for 'you can't blame me'. C2: 'never borrowed' contradicts 'when you lent it to me' and 'I gave it back'; 'already cracked' contradicts 'perfect condition'.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'arguing in the alternative (even if X)': not marked as alternatives; asserted as facts.

error_sentence: the procurement law requires that the same waiver be offered to every builder who asks... So a single waiver would very likely lead to waivers that leave the office without most of its funding.
conditions_met_evidence: C3 NOT met: each link supported - binding legal duty stated, 42 builders, fee funds most of office.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'binding mechanism (a legal duty) shown' applies; LA 'well-supported chains are reasonable'.

error_sentence: My grandfather swore that every time he washed his car, it rained the next day... lost the logbook in a rainstorm, which he considered the final proof.
conditions_met_evidence: No argument by the speaker: the passage reports (with humour) the grandfather's belief. METHOD (g): reporting or satirising someone else's argument is no issue.
lookalikes_ruled_out: n/a
notes: FORCED/CONFLICT: the grandfather's reasoning, taken by itself, would meet post-hoc C1-C3. Rule (g) makes a reported argument no issue. Entries recorded: post-hoc (causal leap), superstitious-thinking considered.

error_sentence: All licensed electricians in this county have passed a safety exam. Everyone on the hospital's maintenance crew is a licensed electrician in this county. So everyone on the maintenance crew has passed a safety exam.
conditions_met_evidence: Valid Barbara syllogism; middle term distributed in the major premise; no syllogism-family condition met.
lookalikes_ruled_out: n/a

error_sentence: But Britain is the parent country, say some. Then the more shame upon her conduct. Even brutes do not devour their young... wherefore the assertion, if true, turns to her reproach
conditions_met_evidence: First reply is a fair reduction from the opponents' own premise (if parent, conduct is worse). No condition of a fallacy met for this step.
lookalikes_ruled_out: Arguing from the opponent's own commitments.
notes: Real text (Paine, Common Sense, 1776). Step 1 legitimate.

error_sentence: but it happens not to be true, or only partly so, and the phrase parent or mother country hath been jesuitically adopted by the king and his parasites, with a low papistical design of gaining an unfair bias on the credulous weakness of our minds.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: 'it happens not to be true, or only partly so' - asserted, not shown within the passage. C2: belief in the phrase explained by a design to exploit 'the credulous weakness of our minds' (bias/psychology of holders and promoters). C3: the explanation follows in place of any showing in the passage.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'explaining why someone holds a view after it has been shown wrong on independent grounds': no independent grounds are given in the passage text.
notes: FORCED/CONFLICT: in the full pamphlet Paine immediately gives independent grounds ('Europe, and not England, is the parent country of America'), which would trigger the look-alike; the excerpt alone forces a flag. Considered appeal-to-motive (same family; motives not offered as why an argument fails but to explain an untrue belief) - bulverism fits better. Loaded words ('parasites','papistical') not a second error (METHOD c); openly evaluative pamphlet.

error_sentence: Nowhere does it mention the cholera outbreak that county records place in the village that summer. So the outbreak never reached the village, and the county records are wrong.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: diary does not mention the outbreak. C2: 'the outbreak never reached the village'. C3 (outside-text, but met from text): 'survives only in fragments' and 'deal almost entirely with baptisms and pew rents' - no strong reason to expect mention.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'source would very likely have mentioned it': no - fragmentary, narrow-topic source.
notes: Also overrides positive contrary evidence (county records) on silence alone; same step, one label (ignorance-and-burden family). Considered argument-from-ignorance: argument-from-silence is the more specific entry.

error_sentence: Someone who has given up everything has no reason to lie, so his prediction that the river will flood next Tuesday must be true.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: 'owns nothing but the clothes on his back'. C2: offered as the reason his prediction 'must be true' - accuracy of a flood forecast is unrelated to money.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'cheapness as indicator of value where it tracks value': no reason poverty tracks forecasting accuracy.
notes: Underlying gap: sincerity (no reason to lie) does not entail accuracy; same step, one label. Considered appeal-to-authority (no expertise claimed), non-sequitur (fallback; more specific entry fits).

error_sentence: All 2,000 vials in lot 7 were filled from the same tank, and that tank tested positive for bacterial contamination before filling. So any given vial from lot 7 has to be treated as contaminated
conditions_met_evidence: division C3 NOT met: reason for carry-over given (every vial filled from the contaminated tank). Conclusion is a precautionary decision ('has to be treated as... until individually tested').
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'properties that do carry down to every member' applies.
notes: Also argument-from-ignorance precaution LA would apply if considered.

error_sentence: I'll be voting on my brother-in-law's development, though, because I know I can be impartial, and the rule is really meant for people who can't be.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: 'Every member... must recuse themselves... that is basic integrity'. C2: exception claimed for own vote. C3: the only reason is self-assessed impartiality ('I know I can be'), which the universal recusal rule exists precisely not to rely on; no supported relevant difference.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'relevant difference is stated and supported': stated, not supported. double-standard LA routes self-exemption to special pleading.
notes: Unclear rule: C3 'no reason relevant to the rule's purpose' - a claim of impartiality is superficially relevant to the purpose; I treat an unsupported self-assessment as not a relevant reason. Text does not explicitly say the speaker has a financial stake in the brother-in-law's development; the 'though' concedes the rule applies.

error_sentence: The Vienna Philharmonic is one of the finest orchestras in the world. Our new neighbor plays in its viola section, so she must be one of the finest violists in the world, and her lessons will be the best in town.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: orchestra 'one of the finest in the world'. C2: member concluded to be 'one of the finest violists in the world'. C3: no reason why the whole's excellence carries to each player.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'properties that carry down by definition': not so.
notes: The further step to 'her lessons will be the best in town' (playing skill -> teaching quality) is an additional unsupported leap; no more specific entry found; kept within this row rather than using the non-sequitur fallback. Charitable note: membership of a top orchestra is real evidence of high skill, but 'must be one of the finest' outruns it.

error_sentence: so it is up to the company to show that with controlled trials. Until it does, the regulator is right to keep the claim off the label, not because the claim has been proven false, but because it hasn't been shown to be true.
conditions_met_evidence: Burden placed on the claimant (misplaced-burden C2 not met). argument-from-ignorance C2 not met: explicitly not concluding falsity; decision only.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA procedural default with conclusion kept to a decision applies.
notes: Correct use of burden of proof.

error_sentence: It is admitted that he did sincerely believe in the soundness of his ship; but the sincerity of his conviction can in no wise help him, because he had no right to believe on such evidence as was before him.
conditions_met_evidence: Moral argument with stated grounds (belief acquired by stifling doubts; knowingly worked into that frame of mind). No entry's conditions met.
lookalikes_ruled_out: n/a
notes: Real text (W. K. Clifford, 'The Ethics of Belief', 1877). Considered begging-the-question (the 'no right to believe' premise is the thesis being illustrated, but it is supported by 'stifling his doubts').

error_sentence: If the forecaster knows that tomorrow's launch will be scrubbed, then the launch will necessarily be scrubbed. And she does know it... So the scrub is necessary, and nothing the engineers do tonight could change it
conditions_met_evidence: C1: knowledge entails truth - a conditional true by definition ('necessarily, if she knows X then X') read as 'if she knows X then necessarily X'. C2: 'she does know it' is merely true (contingent). C3: 'So the scrub is necessary, and nothing the engineers do tonight could change it'.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'P itself shown to be necessary': no.
notes: Second weakness not given a separate row: 'she does know it, because her models are excellent' - excellent models give a reliable forecast, not knowledge; no specific entry fits and fallback not needed.

error_sentence: Management: We've put eight years and $30 million into the current scheduling system. Management: Switching now would throw all of that away, so we're keeping it.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: keep or switch. C2: 'eight years and $30 million'. C3: given as the sole reason ('so we're keeping it').
lookalikes_ruled_out: LAs: no evidence of prospects, commitment, remaining benefit or switching cost given by management.
notes: Union representative's replies are correct reasoning (future costs: $4M vs $1.5M/yr, 40->5 min errors; 'whatever we spent before') - no issue for those steps.

error_sentence: Hospice patients are allowed to take high-dose morphine whenever they ask for it. If that is acceptable for them, there is no good reason pharmacies shouldn't hand out high-dose morphine to anyone who asks.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: hospice patients vs anyone at a pharmacy. C2: permission for hospice patients carried to everyone. C3: relevant differences (terminal illness, pain relief at end of life, medical supervision, addiction/overdose risk to the general public) are common knowledge.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'shared features are the ones that matter': no. LA 'illustration only': no, it argues.
notes: Considered slippery-slope (no chain), double-standard (cases not relevantly alike, which is the point).

error_sentence: Margaret Hale taught chemistry at Westbrook High for 34 years
conditions_met_evidence: No argument: obituary.
lookalikes_ruled_out: n/a
notes: No argument.

error_sentence: A genuine charity, properly understood, is one that spends nothing at all on salaries or advertising. The Riverside Food Bank pays its two staff members and runs radio ads, so it isn't a genuine charity
conditions_met_evidence: C1: 'charity' narrowed to exclude any salaries or advertising, unlike ordinary meaning. C2: builds in the contested evaluation (that overhead disqualifies). C3: presented as neutral ('properly understood') and the conclusion depends on it.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'stipulated technical definition announced and used consistently': not technical; presented as the true meaning. LA 'arguing openly for a revised definition': no argument for it given.
notes: Considered no-true-scotsman (no generalization defended against a counterexample) - persuasive-definition fits better; same family, one label. 'giving to it isn't real giving' is the same step.

error_sentence: The committee approved the spring planting budget of $18,200 by a vote of 4 to 1.
conditions_met_evidence: No argument: meeting minutes.
lookalikes_ruled_out: n/a
notes: No argument.

error_sentence: Calls closed per hour is easy to measure, but it doesn't tell us whether problems were solved. So we'll keep it as one input, and also sample fifty tickets
conditions_met_evidence: C1 met; C3 NOT met: the hard-to-measure factor is explicitly included via sampling and follow-up.
lookalikes_ruled_out: n/a
notes: Correct avoidance of the McNamara fallacy.

error_sentence: None of them mentions renaming Mill Street, so it most likely kept that name through the decade.
conditions_met_evidence: C3 NOT met: minutes 'survive complete' and 'record every street renaming, even trivial ones'.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'source would very likely have mentioned it' applies; hedged 'most likely'.
notes: Archivist's step is legitimate.

error_sentence: But Mill Street can't have been named for a mill; "mill" comes from the Latin molina, a place for grinding grain, and there was never any grinding here, only a sawmill.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: Latin origin 'molina, a place for grinding grain' cited. C2: offered as what 'mill' really means. C3: current usage of 'mill' includes sawmills (common knowledge; the speaker even says 'sawmill'), and the argument relies on the old meaning.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'etymology to explain how a meaning arose': no, used to set present meaning.

error_sentence: So the name must honor some family called Mill.
conditions_met_evidence: C1 met only by implication: after excluding a grain mill, 'must' treats 'family called Mill' as the only remaining origin. C2: the sawmill itself, or other origins (a nearby mill elsewhere, a landmark). C3: conclusion relies on eliminating the one option.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'options really are exhaustive': no.
notes: Possible issue because C1 requires the options to be 'presented'; here the dichotomy is implicit. Settled by whether the implicit two-option framing counts as 'presented'. Could be seen as part of the etymological step.

error_sentence: Cardiologists disagree about whether adults should aim for under 1,500 or under 2,300 milligrams... But both camps agree that... cutting down from the typical 3,400 milligrams lowers blood pressure.
conditions_met_evidence: Conclusion limited to the point experts agree on; disagreement stated honestly. appeal-to-authority C2 not met for the agreed claim.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'genuine experts within their field who broadly agree' applies.

error_sentence: Both groups improved, as very low scorers usually do, but the tutored schools improved by 11 points more on average. That gap, not the raw improvement, is the program's estimated effect.
conditions_met_evidence: regression C3 NOT met: regression explicitly considered; randomized comparison group.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'comparison group that also started extreme shows less change' applies.
notes: Correct reasoning.

error_sentence: If all mankind minus one, were of one opinion... mankind would be no more justified in silencing that one person, than he... would be justified in silencing mankind.
conditions_met_evidence: No entry's conditions met: an argued principle (silencing robs the human race, including dissenters and posterity), not an appeal to numbers; the symmetry claim is supported by the following reason, not by analogy alone.
lookalikes_ruled_out: false-analogy LA: shared feature (silencing an opinion) is the one that matters to the stated reason.
notes: Real text (J. S. Mill, On Liberty, ch. 2, 1859).

error_sentence: Yet the council's landlord-lobby lapdogs, bought and paid for by greedy real-estate barons, voted it down.
conditions_met_evidence: ad-hominem C1/C3 NOT met: no argument by the council is stated or rejected via the insult; the case for assistance rests on the study figures. loaded-language C2/C3 NOT met: openly evaluative, and reasons (38% vs 9%, 60% burdened, reserve fund) are given.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'insult not offered as a reason' (ad-hominem); LA 'openly evaluative writing' (loaded-language).
notes: Unsupported corruption accusation is rude/defamatory but not a reasoning step under the catalog.

error_sentence: The only proof capable of being given that an object is visible, is that people actually see it... In like manner, I apprehend, the sole evidence it is possible to produce that anything is desirable, is that people do actually desire it.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: visible/audible compared with desirable ('In like manner'). C2: the evidential standard for 'visible' (actually seen) is carried to 'desirable' (actually desired). C3: relevant difference - 'visible' means 'can be seen', while 'desirable' in the conclusion ('happiness is a good') means 'worth desiring'; actual seeing settles visibility, actual desire does not settle worth. The conclusion claims 'all the proof... which it is possible to require'.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'shared features are the ones that matter': no, see C3. LA 'illustration only': no, 'In like manner' carries the inference. naturalistic-fallacy LA (arguing that a natural property is a sign of goodness) noted, but the analogy step itself is the faulty part.
notes: Real text (J. S. Mill, Utilitarianism, ch. 4, 1863). Label disputed: textbooks often call this equivocation on '-able' (desirable = can be / ought to be desired). Under charity (b) Mill only claims desire is evidence, so I used false-analogy rather than equivocation. Scholarly defenders contest any fallacy here; the strict reading of the conditions still flags.

error_sentence: each person's happiness is a good to that person, and the general happiness, therefore, a good to the aggregate of all persons.
conditions_met_evidence: C1: property of each member ('each person's happiness is a good to that person'). C2: the whole ('the general happiness... a good to the aggregate of all persons'). C3: no reason given beyond 'therefore'.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'properties that do carry over (like weight)' might apply: if 'good to' is additive (a sum of goods is good to the sum of persons), the step is valid; the text doesn't settle which reading is meant.
notes: Possible issue because a look-alike might apply (METHOD g). Settled by whether 'a good to the aggregate' means a simple sum (fine) or a good each person has reason to desire (composition).

error_sentence: Therefore, any calm person... can see that in the Old Oolitic Silurian Period... the Lower Mississippi River was upwards of one million three hundred thousand miles long
conditions_met_evidence: No argument made in earnest: the passage satirises over-extrapolation ('such wholesale returns of conjecture out of such a trifling investment of fact').
lookalikes_ruled_out: n/a
notes: Real text (Mark Twain, Life on the Mississippi, ch. 17, 1883). METHOD g: satire -> no issue; entry recorded: over-extrapolation.

error_sentence: It has no entry for the brig Henrietta. So the Henrietta probably never called at this port that year
conditions_met_evidence: C3 NOT met: log 'records every arrival and departure, down to fishing boats and coal barges' with 'no gaps' - strong reason to expect mention. Hedged 'probably'.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'source would very likely have mentioned it' applies.

error_sentence: A highwayman holds a pistol to my ear, and mutters through his teeth, "Stand and deliver, or I shall kill you, and then you will be a murderer!"
conditions_met_evidence: false-analogy C3 NOT met: the shared feature (a threat to extort what is one's own, with blame shifted to the victim) is the one the conclusion relies on; speaker addresses the obvious difference (money vs vote) explicitly.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'shared features are the ones that matter' applies.
notes: Real text (Lincoln, Cooper Union address, 1860). The speaker identifies and rebuts the opponents' threat-and-blame move (METHOD g correct identification -> no issue). Records: appeal-to-force (opponents' move), false-analogy (checked).

error_sentence: The word "nice" comes from the Latin nescius, meaning "ignorant." So when my editor called my essay "nice," she was really calling it ignorant
conditions_met_evidence: C1: origin nescius 'ignorant' cited. C2: offered as the 'real' meaning ('she was really calling it ignorant'). C3: current meaning of 'nice' is 'pleasant/good' (common knowledge); the complaint relies on the old meaning.
lookalikes_ruled_out: LA 'etymology explaining how a meaning arose': no.

error_sentence: The chloroform temporarily allays the cough, thereby checking Nature's effort to throw off the dead matter from the lungs.
conditions_met_evidence: appeal-to-nature C3 NOT met: the harm is spelled out by mechanism (cough suppression, opiate masking) rather than by the label 'natural'. Reification C2 NOT met: 'Nature's effort' is figurative shorthand for the body's cough reflex.
lookalikes_ruled_out: appeal-to-nature LA 'natural stands for a specific property separately shown to matter'; reification LA 'figurative/shorthand'.
notes: Real text (Samuel Hopkins Adams, The Great American Fraud, 1905-06). Openly evaluative ('diabolical'); a critique of an ad. Factual medical claims are period-specific; not judged.

error_sentence: It is not seen that as our shopkeeper has spent six francs upon one thing, he cannot spend them upon another.
conditions_met_evidence: Speaker rebuts the broken-window argument by pointing to the unseen alternative use of the money (correct identification of an error, METHOD g).
lookalikes_ruled_out: n/a
notes: Real text (Bastiat, 'That Which Is Seen and That Which Is Not Seen', 1850). MISSING ENTRY: the broken window fallacy (ignoring opportunity cost / 'the unseen') has no catalog entry; nearest are lump-of-labour and suppressed-evidence, neither fits.

error_sentence: The Extension.--This consists in carrying your opponent's proposition beyond its natural limits
conditions_met_evidence: No argument: the passage teaches a debating trick (and its defence).
lookalikes_ruled_out: n/a
notes: Real text (Schopenhauer, The Art of Controversy, Stratagem 1). Entry described: straw-man (extension).

error_sentence: He built three companies and is worth over a billion dollars. So when he says the city's bridge inspections are a waste of money, he's obviously right; you don't get that rich by being wrong.
